evidence: plan_review_T10.md:10 'ONLY these four MAJOR classes warrant severity >= major ... every other finding (cost, observability, drift, sizing, style) is at most minor.'
decide.py:364-410 impact_plan derives priority from _PLAN_SEVERITY_AXES + _PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_FLOOR (0.85), with no T10-class input

Ticket bfa8 description explicitly accepts this: 'Class scoping for T10 is achieved through severity guidance, not a new mechanism ... No pass3_decide changes' — the ticket rejected building a per-class Pass-3 mechanism
advisory.finding: T10 class-scoping to the four MAJOR classes is enforced only as LLM prompt guidance in plan_review_T10.md, not deterministically in Pass-3: impact_plan computes priority from the 7 verifier-emitted plan-severity axes (ac_unverifiable/dod_uncertifiable/undecomposed/divergent_implementation etc. with a 0.85 hard-override floor), independent of any T10 'MAJOR class' taxonomy. A non-MAJOR T10 finding (cost/observability/drift/sizing) whose verifier grades a hard-override axis present could still floor to >=0.85 and BLOCK at the 0.90 bar, contrary to the commit's claim that 'lesser findings cannot reach the 0.90 bar'.
scenarios: An LLM T10 finding on a cost/observability concern is graded by the verifier with, e.g., undecomposed or dod_uncertifiable present, flooring impact to 0.85+ and blocking despite being a non-MAJOR class.
